clue.text: A personal impression that's unique

parts.note: the impression is not an opinion but a mark pressed from a fingertip, which no two people share

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for leaving a one-of-a-kind personal impression on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' suggests the effect someone makes; read literally, it is the inked mark of a digit, unique to each person.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridged pattern of a fingertip, pressed onto a surface, is distinct for every individual.

clue.text: Attempt to hide another wad that is cheap and showy

indicators.note: one word hides another when it wraps round it, so the attempt holds the rest inside
another wad is the same letters made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A plan to conceal a second wad of cash that turns out tacky and flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the anagram signal: a second wad is the same notes reshuffled. 'to hide' is the container signal, with the attempt wrapped round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry goods are gaudy but of poor quality, flashy yet inexpensive.

clue.text: Lou and Tim were troubled during the previous month

indicators.note: the two names, once troubled, are stirred up into a new order of letters

explanation.surface: Two friends, Lou and Tim, had a hard time last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were troubled' scrambles LOU and TIM together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimo is the old business-letter term for last month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ultimo'.

clue.text: Too slow, unable to see the time?

definitions.meaning: running late, lagging behind the correct hour
literally standing at the back of a timepiece, so its face is hidden

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means late or slow, and someone positioned at the rear of a timepiece could not read its face.

clue.text: Produce another photograph?

parts.note: printing a film image a second time is processing it again, though the word usually means rebuilding a site

explanation.surface: A request for a second print of a snapshot.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is rebuilding an area; the question mark points to the darkroom sense of processing film once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop film is to produce prints from it, so doing it again yields a further picture, while the everyday sense is regenerating land.

clue.text: Gets close to a saner disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the word are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is approaching a calmer, more sensible temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, but signals rearranging SANER.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach something is to come nearer to it.

clue.text: This may be in ring given to a friend

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery handed over to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a gemstone that may be set in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone often mounted in jewellery such as a finger band.

clue.text: Sole pair resolved to split into opposing camps

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and reformed, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people alone together decided to divide into rival factions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like 'decided' but signals mixing SOLE and PAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise a group is to divide it into two sharply contrasting factions.

clue.text: Sends Lew off because of an obscenity

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses Lew for using foul language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'sends off', but signals mixing SENDS and LEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecency or crudeness of language or behaviour.

clue.text: One has to be patient with it for a long time

definitions.text: One has to be patient with it for a long time

parts.words: One has to be patient with it for a long time
parts.note: being patient means tolerant, but read as a noun a patient is someone under medical care for a lasting condition

explanation.surface: Advice that something demands lasting patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' seems an adjective meaning tolerant; it is the noun, someone receiving medical treatment over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-lasting disease keeps someone under medical care for years.

clue.text: Keep your eyes on the timekeeper

definitions.meaning: to observe or look at attentively
a small timepiece worn on the wrist

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means observe closely, and the noun is a wristworn timepiece.

clue.text: No-one can recover from such a powerful stroke

definitions.text: No-one can recover from such a powerful stroke

parts.words: No-one can recover from such a powerful stroke
parts.note: a stroke might be a medical seizure, but here it is a blow so heavy it kills

explanation.surface: A warning about a particularly serious medical stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests a medical event; it means a hit, one that proves fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal hit, or figuratively an event that ends something for good.

clue.text: Dynasty of an Italian city half over!

parts.note: Roman means belonging to Rome, the Italian capital

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word means its first two letters only

explanation.surface: An exclamation that half an Italian city is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes OV, the first two letters of 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruling family of Russia from 1613 until the revolution of 1917.

clue.text: Worn before the kilt

parts.note: before means in front of rather than earlier, so this is something hanging at the front of Highland dress

explanation.surface: Something put on prior to donning a kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' suggests time; it means position, the pouch hangs in front of the kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather or fur pouch hung from a belt at the front of Scottish Highland dress.

clue.text: Amorous thief's takings?

parts.note: a romantic robber's haul would be caresses snatched without permission

explanation.surface: Wondering what a lovesick burglar would make off with.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsy: the loot is affectionate gestures taken by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Kisses snatched unexpectedly or furtively, as if taken without leave.

clue.text: There is nothing to equal this apple

definitions.text: There is nothing to equal this

explanation.definitionFit: The word means without equal, and is also the name of an old apple variety.

clue.text: Took back what had been said and retired

definitions.text: Took back what had been said

definitions.meaning: went away or ... from a place

explanation.definitionFit: Someone retracting a remark and someone leaving a room both pulled back.

clue.text: I treated eccentric who did nothing original

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient complains of an odd doctor who only copied others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a noun for the person, but signals scrambling I TREATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat something already said or done is no innovation.

clue.text: Ah, tin-opener I discovered outside

indicators.note: discovered means opened up and laid bare, so the letters are unpacked and set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on finding a can opener out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like 'found', but signals rearranging AH TIN-OPENER I.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of doors, under the sky rather than in a building.

clue.text: Pugnacious cocky little bird

definitions.meaning: small but aggressive, as in bantamweight
a small breed of domestic chicken, the cock being famously feisty

explanation.definitionFit: A small domestic fowl known for its aggression, and the word as an adjective for a little but combative person.

clue.text: The way a nail was mangled by an old leader

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so the letters of the word are disordered

explanation.surface: A road where a nail got bent, attributed to a former dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangled' scrambles only the word nail; 'The way' is the usual street abbreviation, and 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union from the 1920s until 1953.

clue.text: Athlete ruled out within an hour

indicators.note: within means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner was disqualified less than sixty minutes later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on ruled, and 'within' puts that inside the abbreviation for hour; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who races over a series of barriers on a track.

clue.text: Arrest at home after a race

indicators.note: after means the home piece follows the race piece

explanation.surface: A police arrest made at someone's house after they had been out running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the home piece behind the race piece; to run someone in is British slang for arresting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for taking into custody, as an officer hauling someone in.

clue.text: As a minimum, salt and tea were distributed

indicators.note: were distributed means were shared out and scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Condiments and drinks being handed round, at the very least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were distributed' scrambles SALT and TEA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning no fewer or less than, if nothing more.

clue.text: Reserve some diamonds in fashion centre

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another
to fashion is to shape, so the letters of the word are reshaped

explanation.surface: Keeping back jewels in a fashion district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is the anagram signal on centre, and 'in' sets the diamonds inside it; ice is underworld slang for diamonds. 'Reserve' means restraint, not a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as restraint, a tendency to keep thoughts and feelings to oneself.

clue.text: Praise when old tax was reduced by a pound

indicators.note: reduced by means one letter is taken away from the levy

parts.note: a toll is a levy or tax
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Applauding a time when a former levy was cut by a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by' takes one pound sign letter from the tax, leaving three letters after the prefix for old.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or glorify someone or something enthusiastically.

clue.text: Extra spacious

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, giving an extra run

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a ball bowled out of reach gives an extra run; and broad means roomy.

clue.text: One is at home in a castle, so it is said

definitions.text: One is at home in a castle, so it is said

parts.words: One is at home in a castle, so it is said
parts.note: the proverb says a man of England regards his home as his castle

explanation.surface: A saying about who feels at home in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: It turns on the proverb 'an Englishman's home is his castle', meaning his house is his private domain.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that every man of England treats his house as a fortress.
